newsitem.title: GREECE: FOUR BIDS PLACED FOR GREECE'S STATE BANK OF CRETE.
newsitem.headline: FOUR BIDS PLACED FOR GREECE'S STATE BANK OF CRETE.

text.p: A total of four bids for the sale of the state Bank of Crete were submitted on June 6, the bank said in a statement.
The four bidders are Nanjing Star Company Ltd, An Ran Industrial Group Ltd, both incorporated in China, Luxembourg-based Consolidated Eurofinance Holding SA and the Bank of Piraeus .
Consolidated Eurofinance Holding SA is the holding company of the Greek shipping and financial group owned by the Latsis family.
The bank will evaluate bids on June 10, it said.
The minimum price for the Bank of Crete was set at 30 billion drachmas.
Prospective buyers are able to pay the price in one shot or make a minimum downpayment equal to 30 percent of the price and pay the balance in three years.
For the purpose of comparative evaluation of bids, the amount (total or downpayment) will be subject to a bonus of 5.0 percent that will be paid within a month from the acceptance of the tender.

Fifteen percent of the total amount will be placed in an escrow account to compensate for any accounting differences that might emerge after the sale of the bank and for a period of six months from the acceptance of the tender. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
